findings.title: DerivedCalculator.computeAll is monkey-patched at init by the force domain (Skill Focus non-stacking post-filter)
findings.observed: registerForceSuiteRuntimeRepairs (called first in init, index.js:102) replaces DerivedCalculator.computeAll with a wrapper that calls the original and then rewrites the returned updates via suppressDuplicateSkillFocusInUpdates. The canonical derived calculator therefore does not produce the final skill totals by itself; a stacking rule lives in a force-domain patch module, and the wrapper mutates the object returned from the signature cache.
findings.intendedOwnership: Skill/stacking behaviour inside DerivedCalculator/ModifierEngine (A-09 clean cutover; A-01).
findings.proposedSolution: Fold the Skill Focus non-stacking logic into the skill-total computation that DerivedCalculator already calls (or into ModifierEngine stacking for the Skill Focus source), with its existing tests, then delete the wrapper. No change to the stacking result itself; if the intended stacking behaviour is not documented, record it before moving (CLAUDE.md §3).
findings.regressionTests: Golden skill totals with duplicate Skill Focus sources before/after folding; assert DerivedCalculator.computeAll is not reassigned after init.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Character with Skill Focus from two sources, sheet totals.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes a live patch over the core derived pipeline.
findings.risk: Medium: skill totals are visible everywhere.

findings.title: 109 live runtime monkey-patch sites in live modules across 8 owner domains
findings.observed: Live sites by owner domain: feats 32, compat-patches 27, progression 24, talents 11, force 9, infrastructure 3, combat 2, actor-core 1 (instance patch of actor.items). Targets include DerivedCalculator.computeAll, ModifierEngine._getFeatModifiers, SWSEChat.postRoll, DamageSystem.applyPacketToActor, PrerequisiteChecker, AbilityEngine.evaluateAcquisition, TalentStep/ForcePowerStep prototypes, ProgressionFinalizer statics, Document.prototype flag methods. Every live site with its target is listed in dependencies.observedViolations (from = site, to = patched target).
findings.intendedOwnership: Behaviour lives in the owning module; no runtime reassignment (A-09).
findings.proposedSolution: Per owner domain, fold each wrapper body into the target method (or a declared extension registry, e.g. a CombatOptionResolver modifier-source registry) and delete the patch. Order: (1) patches on core authorities (DerivedCalculator.computeAll, ModifierEngine._getFeatModifiers, SWSEChat.postRoll, DamageSystem.applyPacketToActor, ActorEngine), (2) progression step patches, (3) combat option chains, (4) UI patches. Add a CI ratchet that fails on new reassignment sites.
findings.alternatives: Keep patches but centralise installation and assert installation in tests.
findings.regressionTests: For each fold: behaviour parity test that previously ran with the patch installed; census ratchet.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Every class-F patch: live Foundry run of the affected flow.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes parallel execution paths and order dependence.
findings.risk: High if folded without parity tests; combat/progression are runtime-risk areas.

findings.title: Runtime prototype/static monkey-patches of progression steps and prerequisite authorities
findings.observed: At init, TalentStep (_getTalent, _getTalentDescription, _getTalentBenefit, _getTalentPrerequisiteText, _buildCanonicalTalentSelection, _buildPendingAbilityData, _getOwnedTalentKeys, _getTreeInvestmentCount, onStepEnter, _getAvailableTrees, _getTree, _getTalentsForTree), ForcePowerStep._getTelekineticProdigyResolution, FeatStep (_isFeatSelected, _buildPendingAbilityData, _getLegalFeats), PrerequisiteChecker (5 statics) and AbilityEngine.evaluateAcquisition are wrapped by reassignment. Behavior of these classes depends on registration order; reading the class source does not show actual behavior.
findings.intendedOwnership: Each behavior lives in its owning class or an injected strategy (house-rule grant provider, custom-tree provider) that the class calls explicitly.
findings.proposedSolution: Fold each wrapper into its target as an explicit call to a named provider: HouseRuleGrantProvider consulted by PrerequisiteChecker/AbilityEngine/FeatStep/TalentStep; CustomTalentTreeProvider consulted by TalentStep tree lookup; Telekinetic correction moved to talent data (after rules review F-PRG-009). Then delete the patch files and add a CI guard rejecting `.prototype.X =` / `Class.method =` assignments on progression/prerequisite classes.
findings.alternatives: Keep patches but document them in progression-architecture.md (does not satisfy A-09).
findings.regressionTests: Existing feat/talent step tests plus new tests constructing TalentStep/FeatStep without registering patches and asserting house-rule grants and custom trees still appear.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Talent and feat picker with house-rule grants and custom talent trees
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes 3 init-order-dependent execution paths; step behavior readable from source
findings.risk: Medium: wrapper ordering effects (e.g. telekinetic wrapping housekeeping) must be preserved

findings.title: ActorEngine monkey-patches actor.items (filter/some/map/find) on every update, unconditionally
findings.observed: Labelled DEV MODE but not gated: the first updateActor/updateEmbeddedDocuments on an actor replaces four collection methods with wrappers that call SentinelEngine.reportSSOTViolation. With sentinelMode OFF (default) each call returns early; with DEV/STRICT every items.filter (including DerivedCalculator internals) captures a stack trace. This is a runtime monkey-patch (A-09) owned by actor-core.
findings.intendedOwnership: Diagnostics opt-in and non-invasive (A-09).
findings.proposedSolution: Gate instrumentation on SentinelEngine.isEnabled() (or remove it; the census now measures SSOT statically).
findings.regressionTests: Test: with Sentinel OFF, actor.items.filter is the native method after updateActor.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Profile a large actor sheet with Sentinel DEV.

findings.title: combat-ui-behavior-hotfix is a parallel action-execution path (legacy D/F)
findings.observed: Monkey-patches SWSEChat.postRoll; installs a document capture-phase click handler that stopImmediatePropagation()s combat rows to run its own Double/Triple Attack sequence (own full-round spend and rollback) and attack options; applyForcedAttackOption is cloned from combat-feature-handlers; DOM repair/dedupe on every render. FullAttackExecutor already owns double/triple sequencing. Phase-0 doc approves it only as a shrinking bridge.

findings.proposedSolution: Migrate remaining behaviours (multi-attack trigger, option specs, gating) into combat-feature-action-router/FullAttackExecutor, then delete the hotfix and its chat patch.
findings.regressionTests: Double/Triple Attack and Power Attack from sheet produce one spend and same rolls after removal.

findings.regressionTests: Item sheet upgrade button never constructs SWSEUpgradeApp.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Upgrade button on owned and world items.

findings.title: Live runtime monkey-patch chain on combat, grapple, modifier and progression resolvers
findings.observed: Seven live modules replace CombatOptionResolver.collectAttackModifiers, each wrapping the previous; composition depends on registerFeatRuntime order. SWSEGrappling has 8 methods replaced; ModifierEngine._getFeatModifiers, FeatGrantEntitlementResolver (progression) and DamageSystem.applyPacketToActor are replaced too. Legacy class A (active) but violates A-09.
findings.intendedOwnership: Combat/grapple/modifier owners expose declared contributor seams; feats register contributions, not replacements.
findings.proposedSolution: Add contributor registries (CombatOptionResolver.registerAttackContributor, SWSEGrappling feat-rule seam, ModifierEngine feat-modifier provider) and migrate wrappers one family at a time, deleting each patch after parity tests pass.
findings.alternatives: Keep wrappers but centralize them into one ordered composition list with a test asserting the order.
findings.regressionTests: tests/combat-feat-attack-modifier-regression.test.mjs extended to snapshot collectAttackModifiers output for each family before/after migration.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Attack roll breakdown with multiple stacked weapon-style feats matches pre-migration output.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes order-dependent hidden call chain from the attack SSOT path
findings.risk: Behavior drift in attack bonuses if parity is not snapshotted

findings.title: force-suite-runtime-repairs: runtime patches of executor and DerivedCalculator, DOM repairs on every AppV2 render
findings.observed: Live at init: replaces ForceExecutor._getTelepathicIntruderBonus, _generateForcePowerRollMessage, executeForcePower and DerivedCalculator.computeAll (Skill Focus non-stacking applied post hoc to derived updates); repairForceCardIds and repairSkillMathDisplay bound to both renderSWSEV2CharacterSheet and renderApplicationV2, so a character sheet render runs each twice and every other AppV2 render runs the actor lookup. A separate hotfix wraps sheet.render and detects this module by Error().stack. Legacy class F (runtime-risk): it changes execution and derived math.
findings.intendedOwnership: Fixes belong in ForceExecutor, DerivedCalculator/skills (Skill Focus) and the sheet template/context.
findings.proposedSolution: Fold each repair into its owner with a test, then delete the module and the render-guard hotfix; meanwhile drop the duplicate renderApplicationV2 bindings.
findings.regressionTests: Per-repair parity tests.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Force tab actions and skill math display after removal.
findings.simplificationBenefit: Removes a hidden execution layer and stack-sniffing hotfix

findings.title: Document.prototype flag-scope patch affects every document type
findings.observed: getFlag("swse") reads canonical then legacy flags.swse; setFlag("swse") writes canonical. Installed globally for all Documents (also other modules' documents). findings.proposedSolution: Owner decides canonical namespace; migrate persisted flags.swse into it (B-MIG), reroute flags.swse literal reads, then remove both shims.
findings.regressionTests: Round-trip flag tests per document type.
